fotosensibilizare.e: From foto- + sensibilizare. Calque of French photosensibilisation.

pericardectomie.e: Borrowed from French péricardectomie. By surface analysis, pericard + -ectomie.

psihodramatist.e: Borrowed from French psychodramatiste. By surface analysis, psiho- + dramatist.

balmoș.e: Uncertain. Possibly ultimately of Slavic origin; compare bălmăji (“to mix, muddle”), perhaps influenced by valmeș (“mixed, confused”). Compare also the constructions talmeș-balmeș, halmeș-balmeș, and talmeș-halmeș. Recorded variants include balmoj, balmăj, ba…

preliminariamente.e: Borrowed from French préliminairement. By surface analysis, preliminar + -amente.

bazament.e: Borrowed from Italian basamento. By surface analysis, baza + -ment.

preslușnic.e: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic прѣслоушьникъ (prěslušĭnikŭ).

polză.e: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic польза (polĭza).

lotru.e: Unknown. Compare Czech lotr (“rascal, scoundrel”), Polish łotr (“villain, scoundrel”), from German Lotter (“loafer, idler”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *ludraz (“useless; worthless; bad”). Latin latro (“highwayman, bandit”) is thought to be unrelated.
